sample_name: OATutor 2024 help-condition study: first 12 participant summaries
attribution: Pardos, Zachary; Bhandari, Shreya (2023). ChatGPT-generated help produces learning gains equivalent to human tutors on mathematics skills. figshare. Dataset. https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.23935269.v1

sample_file.name: oatutor-real-participants.csv
sample_file.selection: Exact source header and first 12 data records, preserving original bytes and CRLF newlines. No values, columns or records added or altered.

selection_rationale: First 12 source records in published order; includes all three assigned conditions. Convenience demonstration subset, not a representative sample or a new study.
interpretation_limits: These are participant-level study summaries, not a product export or a hint/clickstream log.
condition is the assigned help condition, not proof that a participant opened or received a particular hint.
The participant table supplies no individual inquiry, hint text, event sequence or event timestamps.
preTest, postTest, sessionTime, totalUniqueSteps and learningGain remain original columns and values. No new effect size, pooled score or causal analysis is calculated.
anonUserID is a publisher anonymous participant identifier. Learnlog output replaces the known subject identifier with a scoped HMAC pseudonym. The original public sample remains unchanged.
The published paper states the no-hint control still received correctness feedback and could request a bottom-out answer. The condition label is not evidence of no assistance.
The raw Human tutor condition means human tutor-authored hints, and ChatGPT means pre-generated ChatGPT solution hints. These are not recordings of live human or AI tutoring conversations.
